mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a garage apartment and a standard home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A garage apartment is an accessory dwelling unit built either inside a converted garage or as a second-story addition over a detached or attached garage. In contrast, a standard home addition typically expands the main footprint of the house by adding adjacent ground-floor rooms like living areas or primary bedrooms. The primary tradeoff comes down to vehicle storage and privacy. Converting the garage interior provides ground-level access but removes parking and storage space. Building an apartment above the garage preserves vehicle parking underneath and offers complete privacy from the primary home, though it requires exterior stairs and structural reinforcement for the upper level.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage apartment is a self-contained unit built over or within a garage, while a standard addition directly expands the main home's footprint, often sharing interior access.
